migration.description: Persist the last complete forward proxy subscription result and restore it on service startup.

durable_state.description: The successful parsed proxy URLs and the subscription source list that produced them.
durable_state.storage_implementation: One additive JSON column on the singleton forward_proxy_settings row. Snapshot writes are conditional on the configured source list; a SQLite trigger clears the snapshot whenever that list changes. Shutdown rollback restores settings and the matching snapshot in one transaction.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: The origin/main schema at bc5258f74e61d976adabe1986e49aee773533df5, before the snapshot column.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Candidate branch th/forward-proxy-subscription-recovery; final candidate revision is bound by delivery evidence.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Add subscription_snapshot_json as TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'; the schema initializer is idempotent and does not rewrite existing settings rows.
Install a trigger that clears subscription_snapshot_json when subscription_urls_json changes, including writes from an older same-line binary.

dml_changes.description: After every configured subscription source succeeds, replace the snapshot conditionally against the still-current source list. A fully successful empty aggregate writes an empty node list; all-source or partial failures do not write or apply results.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: No historical backfill is performed because existing runtime rows intentionally omit complete endpoint URLs for some subscription protocols; an incomplete reconstruction would be unsafe. The first successful post-upgrade refresh establishes the durable snapshot.

progress_signals: Presence of the subscription snapshot column and invalidation trigger
Snapshot source list matches the current subscription settings
Active subscription node count after startup restore and refresh
pause_points: After additive schema installation and before the first subscription refresh
After each successful complete subscription refresh snapshot write

recovery.program_rollback_state_behavior: An older same-line binary ignores the additive snapshot column; its subscription source updates fire the retained trigger and clear the snapshot. The old binary does not restore cached nodes itself.
recovery.faulty_release_recovery: A later compatible binary validates snapshot sources before restore and replaces state only after a complete successful refresh.
recovery.interrupted_settings_update_recovery: When route synchronization is interrupted by shutdown, the previous settings and snapshot are restored in one SQLite transaction. If that transaction fails, it rolls back as a unit and the manager remains aligned with the last committed database settings.

required_test_evidence: An existing schema without the column upgrades idempotently and receives the empty default.
A restarted manager restores a source-matched snapshot before refresh; failed and partial refreshes preserve it.
A complete successful empty refresh clears active nodes and durable state immediately.
Changing the source list, including through a legacy-style SQL update, clears the snapshot.
An interrupted settings update restores the old settings and snapshot atomically, and a failed rollback transaction leaves database and manager state aligned.
